[aparasher] Good point. I think they are selling them as a pack of 2 or 3 and adding individual battery to a pack of 2 makes it more expensive than a pack of 3, but you could buy 4 for extra $20. Same is for the other 4AH (bigger in size) as a pack of 2 costs $39, but pack of 3 is $99.
[Daniel Plainview] Like most of the tool companies, Ozito are doing anything but be clear with customers about the real benefits for consumers of their myriad of battery offerings. In short, these 4Ah sealed ones are really only beneficial if you plan to use in wet or very dusty conditions - they are also a tad more compact and lighter than the standard 4Ah ones - which come up for 3 for $99 from time to time.
Credit to whoever found it but the info on the various PXC batts is very handy:
Battery Max W Approx current at 18V Energy
2.0Ah 450W 25A 36Wh
2.5Ah 720W 40A 45Wh
3.0Ah 900W 50A 54Wh
3.0Ah sealed 900W 50A 54Wh
4.0Ah 900W 50A 72Wh
4.0Ah sealed 900W 50A 72Wh
5.2Ah Plus / Ultra 1260W 70A 93.6Wh
6.0Ah Max / 4-6Ah Multi 1350W 75A 108Wh in 6Ah mode
8.0Ah Max / 5-8Ah Multi 1350W 75A 144Wh in 8Ah mode
The 5.2Ah twin pack is the current 'bargain' buy (using the $50 off trade in an old battery promo that runs through to 19OCT26) - to bring the price to $129 for two batts as it has a significant wattage output increase over the common standard 4Ah and many of the PXC tools benefit from this - but many of them don't i.e don't need the extra power, so will perform just the same.
Most of the basic batts in the PXC range use 18650 cells, the 5.2Ah ones use 20650's.
It will be interesting to see what Einhell Pro sell their tabless 4Ah ones for when they get into Bunnings soon - 'Tabless' is a new battery tech and offers significant benefits in battery packs - while only hold 4Ah these will put out 2000w, which is right up there with top end offerings from the top tier companies products - but I expect they'll be ~$150 each or so.
https://www.einhellpro.com.au/p/3001330-pxc-18v-4ah-tabless-…
The bottomline is match the right battery selection to your tools and you will get the best results i.e 5.2Ah in low end PXC blower is of little benefit, but the brushless mowers and trimmers etc will perform much better. :-)
